text:
Ethan Park: Quick question on control-plane semantics for the new provisioning pipeline. State machine is `Requested -> Provisioning -> Imaging -> Bootstrapping -> Validating -> Ready/Failed`. Routing integration (PR-48234) currently only advertises pools in `Ready`. Do we want routing to treat `Validating` as usable capacity (maybe with a low weight) or strictly keep it out until `Ready`?

Mina Haddad: +1 raising this. My gut: keep it OUT. Validating is where we run smoke + perf-canary and we’re still finding real issues (DNS/TLS, ECC, mis-pinned helm values). If we route any prod traffic there we’ll get noisy partial failures and it’ll be hard to reason about.

Ravi Menon: Agree w/ Mina. From routing POV, "usable" needs to mean we can rely on it for SLOs. If we want pre-warm/early traffic, we should define a separate explicit mode (like canary-only) rather than overloading Validating.

Priya Natarajan: +1. Semantics should be boring. `Ready` == safe to route customer traffic. Everything before that is control-plane-owned validation.

Ethan Park: The pushback I’m getting from Infra is that perf-canary + warmup can take 10-20m depending on SKU/region and they’d like to start draining real traffic sooner to reduce end-to-end time-to-ready.

Rafael Mendes: From SRE angle: please don’t. That 10-20m is literally the safety gate. We had a pilot last week where perf-canary would have failed but the pool looked "fine" otherwise. If routing had seen it, we’d have thrown 5xx.

Benji Okafor: Also config validation/policy gates happen before control plane marks `Validating`, but we still do runtime smoke tests there. Treating `Validating` as routable breaks the mental model + makes break-glass overrides riskier.

Jordan Lee: If we *must* do something, we can add an explicit `ready_candidate=true` (or separate state) that requires an opt-in allowlist + audit log. But default should be strict: routing consumes `Ready` only.

Vikram Singh: One more detail: pool registration / dataplane health signals can lag a bit. During Validating, nodes are coming up, agents registering, certs being issued, etc. We’ll see flapping. Routing should not have to handle that.

Aisha Bello: For metrics: time-to-ready includes Validating. If we start routing during Validating, we’ll get into weird territory where time-to-ready is "not done" but capacity is "in use". Hard to communicate to CS/Sales.

Ethan Park: Makes sense. Let’s lock semantics as: `Ready` is the only routable state. `Validating` is explicitly not routable. If infra wants earlier warmup, that needs a separate mechanism that doesn’t involve customer traffic.

Mina Haddad: :thumbsup: Works for me. Can we add something to PR-48234 to make it impossible to accidentally treat Validating as Ready? e.g. explicit enum allowlist + metric counter for rejected states.

Ravi Menon: I can add a guard in routing config ingestion: only accept `[Ready]`, log + metric if anything else shows up. Also add a dashboard note so oncall knows why a pool isn’t being advertised.

Priya Natarajan: Decision recorded here: routing only uses `Ready`. Follow-up: Ethan to update control-plane docs + state machine comments, Ravi to add the routing guard + metric, and Aisha to ensure dashboards label states clearly (Validating != usable).

Ethan Park: Cool. I’ll add a short note to the Ready semantics section + link this thread in the Confluence runbook. Also will ping Vanessa/Irene so infra is aligned.

Rafael Mendes: Thanks. Also please ensure Ready transition is atomic w/ perf-canary completion (we had that race in an earlier build). If you need SRE review on that part, tag me.

Ethan Park: Yep, noted. I’ll make sure PR includes a transactional check (no Ready until perf-canary finished + all checks green).
